name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,273

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Space over capital, which repeats in frieze?

definitions.text: Space over capital, which repeats in frieze?

blocks.note: surface reading: a gap above a capital letter, or a space above a capital city
setter's reading: in a Doric building, the square panel sitting above the column tops, alternating with triglyphs along the frieze

explanation.walkthrough: The capital here is the head of a column, not a letter or a city; in the Doric order the frieze above is divided into repeating square panels.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical architecture this is the panel between two triglyphs in a Doric frieze, lying above the column heads and repeated along its length.

clue.text: Pinko chaps against interrupting Arab leader

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so the word for against goes inside the leader's title

blocks.note: chaps are men
an Arab chief
V for versus

explanation.surface: Leftish men protest against an Arab ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinko looks like an adjective describing the chaps, but it is the definition, used as a noun for a mild leftist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mensheviks were the moderate wing of Russian socialism, so a member is a mild leftist, which is what pinko loosely means.

clue.text: Relatively young crater yet encompassing younger crater’s peaks

indicators.note: peaks are the tops of things, so only the leading letters of the two words are taken
to encompass is to surround, so the word for yet wraps round the selected letters

blocks.note: tho' is a short form of though, meaning yet
initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A geologist compares the ages of two lunar craters.
explanation.walkthrough: Tho' is an informal spelling of though, which can mean yet; the word crater is used twice, once in the definition and once as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tycho is a prominent lunar crater, geologically young at around a hundred million years, with bright rays across the Moon's surface.

clue.text: Try leaving domestic fowl and assume rook cracks shoulder-plate

indicators.note: the word try departs, so its letters are removed from the poultry word
something that cracks a thing gets inside it, so the chess piece goes within the verb

blocks.note: farmyard birds
taken as written, then removed
to don clothes is to put them on
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A cook gives up on chickens while a crow damages a piece of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook looks like the bird, but here it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauldron is the piece of plate armour covering a knight's shoulder; this is an older variant spelling.

clue.text: Composer of film about return of half-forgotten Wagner festival

indicators.note: half of the festival name is forgotten, so only its first half survives
a return goes back the way it came, so the remaining letters are read backwards
about means around, so the word for film wraps round the reversed letters

blocks.note: a film is a thin skin, as on boiled milk
the annual Wagner opera festival in Bavaria

explanation.surface: A documentary about a revival of a half-remembered opera festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Bayreuth, the Bavarian town where Wagner built his opera house, hosts the festival; only its first four letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Skryabin was a Russian composer and pianist; this is a common transliteration of his surname, also written Scriabin.

clue.text: Light boots and silk hotel uniform on man accepting post

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the barrister's letters hold the word for post

blocks.note: a silk is a senior barrister, a King's Counsel, from the silk gown worn
the post is the mail
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
he, a male person

explanation.surface: A man in hotel uniform wearing light boots and silk takes in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: Silk looks like fabric beside uniform, but in Britain a silk is a senior barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Kletterschuhe is German for climbing shoes: light boots with soft soles worn by rock climbers.

clue.text: Name of violinist striking feet in long barbarian cacophony

indicators.note: to strike off the feet is to cut off the bottom ends, so each down word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to yen is to long for
the Huns were barbarian invaders
a racket

explanation.surface: A violinist plays a long, barbaric noise.
explanation.walkthrough: YEN, HUN and DIN each lose their final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yehudi Menuhin was a famous American-born British violinist, so this forename identifies him.

clue.text: Turning up in the part of sandwich containing bone, a wild pig

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the sandwich word wraps round the bone and the a
in a down clue, turning up means reading the whole sequence from bottom to top

blocks.note: an actor appearing in the part of Hamlet is playing as Hamlet
a sub is a submarine sandwich
a rib is a bone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something unexpected shows up in a sandwich: a bone, and a wild boar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue turning up means the assembled letters read from the bottom; in the part of is the theatre sense of as.
explanation.definitionFit: The babirussa is a wild swine of Sulawesi whose upper tusks grow up through the snout and curve back.

clue.text: We are Newton, conversely striving

indicators.note: conversely means the other way round, so the three short words are placed in the opposite order

blocks.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
the singular form of are
the object form of we

explanation.surface: We are Newton, says a team striving to match the scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Conversely here swaps the order of the three words, not the letters within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisus is Latin for effort, used in English for a striving or impulse toward a goal.

clue.text: Owlet caught New Zealand bird in curve downward

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the cricket abbreviation and the bird go within the word for a bow

blocks.note: a nod is a downward bend of the head
C for caught in cricket scores
the tui is a New Zealand honeyeater

explanation.surface: A young owl swoops down to catch a New Zealand bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Owlet looks like a young owl, but it is also a name for a kind of moth.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is also a moth of the noctuid family, many of which have owl-like eyes that shine at night.

clue.text: Perishes stateside, making case for soulless doctor’s ill-fated day

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the dying phrase wraps round the doctor's name

blocks.note: dies in US: perishes in America
Doctor Faust sold his soul to the Devil

explanation.surface: A doctor who sold his soul meets an unlucky end in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlowe's Doctor Faustus sold his soul to Mephistopheles; the phrase dies in US is split to hold his shorter name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase dies infaustus means an unlucky or inauspicious day, a day of bad omen.

clue.text: Cry “what jerks”, backing youth in Greece

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

blocks.note: to sob is to cry
eh? asks what? when you have not heard
physical jerks are exercises, PE being physical education

explanation.surface: Someone cries what jerks while supporting a Greek youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: SOB EH PE read backwards gives EPHEBOS. Physical jerks is old British slang for keep-fit exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece an ephebos was a young man of about eighteen undergoing military and civic training.

clue.text: The reader almost breaks concealed bone in neck

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
to break into something is to enter it, so the shortened word goes inside

blocks.note: past tense of hide
the reader is the person addressed as you

explanation.surface: A reader breaks a hidden bone in their neck.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaks looks like fracturing a bone, but it signals one word entering another.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyoid is a U-shaped bone in the front of the neck that supports the tongue.

clue.text: Embryonic layers developing stem cell without lines and rod

indicators.note: without means lacking, so both instances of the line abbreviation are taken out
something developing changes form, so the letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biology lab describes embryonic tissue developing from stem cells.
explanation.walkthrough: STEM CELL minus LL leaves STEMCE, which with ROD is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The ectoderm is the outermost of the three germ layers of an embryo, giving rise to skin and nerves.

clue.text: Injecting liquid iodide, modify log for observation

indicators.note: something liquid flows and takes new shapes, so these letters are rearranged
to inject is to put inside, so the jumbled letters go within the verb

blocks.note: its letters rearranged
to vary is to change

explanation.surface: A medical log notes an iodide injection being adjusted for monitoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A video diary is a personal record kept on camera, a log that others can watch.

clue.text: Quip I deem funny in place of earlier rider?

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian thinks a joke funny, in place of an earlier performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a rider's place is the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A demipique was an eighteenth-century saddle with a low peak, the seat of a horseman in former times.

clue.text: Mountain of bones

blocks.note: first meaning: a peak in Thessaly, Greece
second meaning: plural of the Latin anatomical word os, a bone

explanation.surface: A mountain made of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Giants in Greek myth piled Pelion on this Thessalian peak, and anatomists use the Latin plural of os for bones.

clue.text: Subsequent bridge system united most of broad

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: Acol is a bidding system in contract bridge, named after a London street
U for united, as in football club names
a broad accent is a thick one

explanation.surface: A bridge player describes a later bidding system agreed by most players.
explanation.walkthrough: THICK loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoluthic means following or attending, from the Greek for follower, so it describes what comes after.

clue.text: Greek giant dog’s destruction welcomed by tailless rodent

indicators.note: without a tail, so the last letter of the animal is cut off
someone welcomed is taken in, so the destruction word goes inside

blocks.note: a small rodent
ruin, as in loss of life

explanation.surface: A giant dog destroys things, then is greeted by a mouse without a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Greek giant dog is the whole definition: the breed was large, not a mythical giant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Molossus was a large mastiff-type hunting dog bred by the Molossians of ancient Epirus in Greece.

clue.text: One’s about to follow Egyptian spirit or Japanese one

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the contraction is read backwards

blocks.note: in Egyptian religion the ka is a person's spiritual double
one is I, and one's is I'm

explanation.surface: A comparison of Egyptian and Japanese spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The one in the definition is a spirit, echoing the Egyptian spirit before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kami are the gods or divine spirits worshipped in Shinto, Japan's native religion.

clue.text: Fiend in charge stops ogreish princess getting into trouble

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the charge abbreviation is put inside the princess's name
getting into something means entering it, so the princess goes inside the trouble word

blocks.note: fuss, as in much ado
Princess Fiona in the film Shrek turns into an ogre
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A demon in charge stops a monstrous princess from getting into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiend looks like a demon, but it is the sense of an enthusiast; the ogreish princess is from the animated film Shrek.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend can mean a fanatic or devotee, as in a fresh-air fiend, which is an aficionado.

clue.text: Deep home insulation material, perhaps

blocks.note: at home is in
felt is one example of insulating material, as in roofing felt

explanation.surface: Thick insulation material for the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Infelt is an old word for heartfelt or inward, describing feelings that run profoundly within.

clue.text: Fiend, not quite without justification, skinned fum, a mythical bird

indicators.note: not quite means a little short, so the last letter is dropped
skinning strips off the outside, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
unduly means unwarrantedly
the fum is the Chinese phoenix

explanation.surface: A demon unjustly flays a phoenix, a creature of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDULY loses the Y and FUM loses F and M.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern African folklore the impundulu is the lightning bird, a vampiric creature linked to witchcraft and storms.

clue.text: Prayer leader with one answer breaking silence

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the answer letter goes within the silence word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
mum is silence, as in keep mum
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: An imam breaks the silence with an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside MUM, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaum, a variant of imam, leads the congregational prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Computer geeks regularly ignored, now thankful

indicators.note: every other letter is passed over in a steady pattern, leaving the alternate ones

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Geeks who were long ignored are now grateful.
explanation.definitionFit: Otaku is a Japanese term for obsessive fans, especially of anime, manga and computing, roughly nerds.

clue.text: Ancient spook in CIA ultimately following every other in Le Carré

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the agency is used
every other means taking alternate letters from the author's name

blocks.note: the last letter
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An old spy in the CIA follows the pattern of a John le Carré novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Spook is a verb here, to frighten, not a noun meaning spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Afear is an archaic verb meaning to frighten, and to spook someone is to scare them.

clue.text: Possibly gifted property that Jacques Tati exhibits

indicators.note: to exhibit is to put on show, so the answer is on display within the name

blocks.note: letters inside the film director's name

explanation.surface: A French film-maker shows off a valuable bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an acquest is property gained other than by inheritance, for instance by purchase or as a gift.

clue.text: Scottish girl set to work with help

indicators.note: putting things to work means rearranging them into action, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young Scotswoman gets down to work with some assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Elspeth is the traditional Scots form of the given name Elizabeth, borne by many women in Scotland.

clue.text: Joined line in revolution against very regal movement

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a seam is the line where two pieces are joined
against, as in back to back
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A line of protesters joins a revolution against a very royal procession.
explanation.walkthrough: Movement is a musical term here, not a march.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is an Italian musical direction meaning majestic, used to mark a stately passage or movement.

clue.text: French con artist is in Barcelona with mugger, say

blocks.note: es is the Spanish and Catalan for is
the mugger is an Indian crocodile, so it is an example of a croc

explanation.surface: A French swindler on the loose in Barcelona with a street robber.
explanation.walkthrough: The mugger here is a reptile, the marsh crocodile of India, not a street thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Escroc is the French word for a swindler or crook, borrowed into English dictionaries.
